release.content: pubrules 0.48.0 was released on 2026-11-20 from commit 8eeac9c96b115814692d58dce004047f1c5f80c4 with these changes.

rows: sync, and so bump, pins pubtest in tests/requirements.txt from the lock only when the lock's is one requirements-pubrules.txt takes (pubtest>=0.2.2); a lock of an older pubrules gave pubtest 0.2.1, which no lock resolved, and now the release state's or latest release is pinned instead

pubrules' own suite runs on pubtest 0.3.0, its record/replay harness among it; the floor every suite's requirements-pubrules.txt names stays pubtest>=0.2.2, so a repository whose features still use a step 0.3.0 removed keeps 0.2.2 until it moves, and the nightly moves the rest
The nightly's provider scenarios no longer read GitHub's latest releases, which moved pubtest's pin once 0.3.0 was out and so locked once too often

a release's wheel is pinned by the name the release gives it, which may differ from its repository (pubtest's PyPI name is pubtestrules): sync, new and the nightly read the file name from the release (or the release state's new `wheel` field) and name the requirement by its distribution; requirements-pubrules.txt no longer requires `pubtest>=X`, which would resolve PyPI's unrelated pubtest beside a pubtestrules pin, and `sync --check` instead fails on a pin older than that floor

sync pins no pubtest in pubtest's own repository (its pyproject.toml registers the pubtest pytest plugin): its suite runs on its checkout, and a pinned release would be a second distribution of the same package once pubtest's is pubtestrules
